enum ClientErrorCode : int64_t {

    kOk = 0, // success
    kIgnore = 1,

    // 1. config error,

    kEmptyConfigParameter = 1002,
    kMismatchVersion = 1003,
    kInvalidTimezone = 1004,
    kInvalidByteSize = 1005,
    kInvalidIPAddr = 1006,
    kInvalidLogLevel = 1007,

    // 2. Auth error
    kWrongPasswd = 2001,
    kInsufficientPrivilege = 2002,

    // 3. syntax error or access rule violation
    kInvalidUsername = 3001,
    kInvalidPasswd = 3002,
    kInvalidDbName = 3003,

    kDroppingUsingDb = 3033,
    kSessionNotFound = 3034,
    kRecursiveAgg = 3035,
    kFunctionArgsError = 3036,
    kImportFileFormatError = 3037,
    kDataNotExist = 3038,
    kColumnCountMismatch = 3039,
    kEmptyDbName = 3040,
    kEmptyTableName = 3041,
    kEmptyColumnName = 3042,
    kEmptyIndexName = 3043,
    kExceedDBNameLength = 3044,
    kExceedTableNameLength = 3045,
    kExceedColumnNameLength = 3046,
    kExceedIndexNameLength = 3047,
    kNoColumnDefined = 3048,
    kNotSupportedTypeConversion = 3049,
    kEmptySelectFields = 3050,
    kInvalidDataType = 3051,
    kParseMatchExprFailed = 3052,
    kFTSIndexNotExist = 3053,
    kUnknownFTSFault = 3054,
    kInvalidConstraintType = 3055,
    kInvalidKnnDistanceType = 3056,
    kInvalidEmbeddingDataType = 3057,
    kInvalidConstantType = 3058,
    kInvalidParsedExprType = 3059,
    kInvalidIndexType = 3060,
    kInvalidIndexParam = 3061,
    kLackIndexParam = 3062,
    kInvalidFilterExpression = 3063,
    kMultipleFunctionMatched = 3064,
    kInsertWithoutValues = 3065,
    kInvalidConflictType = 3066,

    // 4. Txn fail
    kTxnRollback = 4001,
    kTxnConflict = 4002,

    // 5. Insufficient resource or exceed limits
    kDiskFull = 5001,
    kOutOfMemory = 5002,
    kTooManyConnections = 5003,
    kConfigurationLimitExceed = 5004,
    kQueryIsTooComplex = 5005,

    // 6. Query intervention
    kQueryCancelled = 6001,
    kQueryNotSupported = 6002,
    kClientClose = 6003,

    // 7. System error
    kIOError = 7001,
    kDuplicatedFile = 7002,
    kConfigFileError = 7003,
    kLockFileExists = 7004,
    kFileCorrupted = 7005,
    kDataCorrupted = 7006,
    kIndexCorrupted = 7007,
    kFileNotFound = 7008,
    kDirNotFound = 7009,
    kDataIOError = 7010,
    kUnexpectedError = 7011,
    kCheckpointing = 7029,

    // 8. meta error
    kInvalidEntry = 8001,
    kNotFoundEntry = 8002,
    kEmptyEntryList = 8003,
};
objects.description: Error code enumeration used by the Infinity client to classify client- and server-side failures and statuses. Backed by int64_t and grouped by functional areas.
Lightweight status object returned by client APIs, containing an error code and message. Provides convenience methods to check success and retrieve details.

objects.definition: enum CreateOption : int8_t { kErrorIfExists = 0, kIgnoreIfExists = 1, kReplaceIfExists = 2 };
objects.description: Create-time behavior flags for resources (e.g., databases, tables): error, ignore if exists, or replace.
Drop-time behavior options specifying whether to error or ignore when the target does not exist.
Simple descriptor of a database including its name and storage path.
Descriptor of a table with identifying fields and basic statistics (counts of columns, segments, rows) and storage path.
Primary client class encapsulating a Thrift connection/session to an Infinity service. Manages transports/protocol, offers database/table management APIs, and stores a session id.

functions.name: infinity::client::ClientStatus::OK
functions.description: Return a success ClientStatus instance. Intended as a convenience factory for callers that need to indicate success without an error message.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::Connect
functions.signature: static infinity::client::Client Connect(const std::string &ip_address, uint16_t port);
functions.description: Establish a client connection to an Infinity service at the given IP address and port, creating a session-backed Client object. Usage: call once to obtain a Client, then use the returned instance for further operations (databases, tables, etc.).
requirements: ip_address should be a valid IP address string (IPv4/IPv6); empty strings are invalid (inferred from name/signature).
port must be a valid TCP port number in the range 0–65535 (inferred).

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::Disconnect
functions.description: Close the underlying transport/session for this Client. Typically called when finished with the Client to free resources and end the session.
requirements: Must be called on a Client that was successfully connected/initialized (inferred).
After disconnecting, the Client instance should not be used for further RPCs (inferred).

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::CreateDatabase
functions.description: Create a database with the given name, honoring the specified creation option (error, ignore, or replace if exists). Returns a status indicating success or the reason for failure.
requirements: db_name must be non-empty (inferred from typical API semantics).
create_option controls existence behavior and must be one of: kErrorIfExists, kIgnoreIfExists, kReplaceIfExists.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::DropDatabase
functions.description: Drop the specified database, honoring the provided drop option when the database may not exist. Returns a status indicating success or failure.
requirements: drop_option must be either kErrorIfNotExists or kIgnoreIfNotExists.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::ListDatabases
functions.description: Retrieve the list of database names visible to/accessible by the current session.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::ShowDatabase
functions.description: Fetch descriptive information (name, storage path) about a specific database.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::CreateTable
functions.signature: infinity::client::ClientStatus CreateTable(const std::string &table_name, std::vector<infinity_thrift_rpc::ColumnDefinition> &columns, const infinity_thrift_rpc::TableProperties &table_properties, infinity::client::CreateOption create_option = infinity::client::CreateOption::kErrorIfExists);
functions.description: Create a table with the given name, column definitions, and table properties. Creation behavior when the table exists is controlled by create_option. Returns a status indicating success or failure.
requirements: columns must define at least one column and must be properly initialized (inferred from function purpose).
table_properties must be a valid, initialized set of properties suitable for table creation (inferred).
create_option must be one of: kErrorIfExists, kIgnoreIfExists, kReplaceIfExists.

functions.name: infinity::client::Client::DropTable
functions.description: Drop the specified table, honoring the provided drop option if the table may not exist. Returns a status indicating success or failure.
requirements: drop_option must be either kErrorIfNotExists or kIgnoreIfNotExists.

functions.description: List the names of tables within the specified database.

functions.description: Retrieve detailed information (database, name, storage path, column/segment/row counts) about a specific table.

data_types.description: A generic string that must have length >= 1. No specific format constraints (can contain arbitrary bytes/characters). Used for identifiers such as database or table names where an empty value is invalid.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (non-empty string) calls.
# The target stubs request database/table names with length >= 1 and no other
# strict formatting. However, to exercise different code paths in typical
# database systems, we generate a variety of identifier-like and path-like
# strings, including:
# - simple alphanumerics
# - names with Unicode
# - names with special characters commonly seen in identifiers
# - names that look like filesystem paths
# - boundary-length names (very short and relatively long but < 4096)
# - names with dots, dashes, spaces, quotes, backslashes, SQL-ish punctuation
# - names that may collide (same name twice) to exercise create/drop options
#
# The returned buffer is a single string instance. The harness may split or
# reuse the buffer for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls depending on integration,
# but each call in the listed stubs only requires a non-empty arbitrary string.

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_LETTERS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
DIGITS = "0123456789"
IDENT_CHARS = ASCII_LETTERS + DIGITS + "_"
SPECIALS = "- .:$@#()[]{}!%^&*+,;='\"`~|?<>\\/"
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "Δ", "λ", "漢字", "😀", "ñ", "ö", "ß", "Ж", "ح", "ह", "한", "字",
]

# Some interesting base names to mix in
BASE_NAMES = [
    "db", "table", "prod", "dev", "test", "tmp", "backup", "archive",
    "users", "orders", "metrics", "logs", "session", "cache", "config",
]

PATH_PREFIXES = ["/var/lib/", "/tmp/", "C:/data/", "../", "./", "~/"]
PATH_SEPARATORS = ["/", "\\\\"]

def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure first char is not a digit to mimic common identifier rules
    first = rng.choice(ASCII_LETTERS + "_")
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(max(0, n-1)))
    return first + rest

def _rand_with_specials(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = IDENT_CHARS + SPECIALS
    s = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid empty after trimming; ensure non-empty
    if not s:
        s = rng.choice(BASE_NAMES)
    return s

def _rand_unicode_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII, specials, and Unicode samples
    pools: List[str] = [IDENT_CHARS, SPECIALS] + UNICODE_SAMPLES
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        pool = rng.choice(pools)
        # If pool is a multi-char string, pick one char; if it's a unicode token
        if pool in (IDENT_CHARS, SPECIALS):
            out.append(rng.choice(pool))
        else:
            out.append(pool)
    s = "".join(out)
    # Ensure length >= 1
    return s if s else rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)

def _rand_path_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = rng.choice(PATH_PREFIXES)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        part_kind = rng.randrange(3)
        if part_kind == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_identifier(rng, 1, 8))
        elif part_kind == 1:
            parts.append(_rand_with_specials(rng, 1, 8).strip())
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(BASE_NAMES))
    sep = rng.choice(PATH_SEPARATORS)
    # If Windows-style, keep drive colon intact
    body = sep.join(p for p in parts if p)
    return prefix + body

def _rand_dot_qualified(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # e.g., db.schema.table or just db.table
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 3)):
        choice = rng.randrange(3)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(_rand_identifier(rng, 1, 16))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(rng.choice(BASE_NAMES))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_unicode_name(rng, 1, 4))
    return ".".join(parts)

def _rand_quoted(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Return a name wrapped in various quoting styles common in SQL/paths
    inner = _rand_with_specials(rng, 1, 24)
    style = rng.choice(["'", '"', "`", "[]", "{}", "()"])
    if style == "[]":
        return "[" + inner + "]"
    if style == "{}":
        return "{" + inner + "}"
    if style == "()":
        return "(" + inner + ")"
    return style + inner + style

def _boundary_length_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate near-maximum name but keep total buffer <= MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
    # Limit name length to 1024 to be safe and practical
    n = rng.randint(64, 1024)
    # Use a safe alphabet to avoid excessive multi-byte expansion
    return _rand_with_specials(rng, n, n)

def _catalog_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce names commonly seen as database/table names
    base = rng.choice(BASE_NAMES)
    suffix_choice = rng.randrange(6)
    if suffix_choice == 0:
        return base
    if suffix_choice == 1:
        return f"{base}_{rng.randint(0, 9999)}"
    if suffix_choice == 2:
        return f"{base}-{rng.choice(['v1','v2','beta','alpha','canary'])}"
    if suffix_choice == 3:
        return f"{base}{rng.choice(['2024','2025'])}{rng.randint(1,12):02d}{rng.randint(1,28):02d}"
    if suffix_choice == 4:
        return f"{base}.{rng.choice(['raw','stg','dim','fact'])}"
    return base.upper()

def _assemble_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        _rand_identifier(rng, 1, 24),
        _rand_with_specials(rng, 1, 48),
        _rand_unicode_name(rng, 1, 24),
        _rand_path_like(rng),
        _rand_dot_qualified(rng),
        _rand_quoted(rng),
        _boundary_length_name(rng),
        _catalog_like(rng),
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many distinct strings to include in the buffer. Some harnesses
    # reuse a single buffer per FUZZ_PARAM_STR call; others may split by NUL or
    # newline. To be broadly useful, we produce multiple candidates separated by
    # newlines and NULs so frameworks can pick either whole or split tokens.
    count = rng.randint(3, 10)

    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        s = rng.choice(_assemble_candidates(rng))
        # Ensure non-empty and reasonable size after UTF-8 encoding
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')
        if not b:
            b = b"x"
        # Truncate overly long parts to keep total under MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
        if len(b) > 1024:
            b = b[:1024]
        parts.append(b)
        # Add separators: alternate newline and NUL to help different consumers
        sep = b"\n" if rng.randrange(2) == 0 else b"\x00"
        parts.append(sep)

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    if len(blob) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    # Guarantee at least one byte and that it doesn't end with a separator to
    # avoid empty last token in some parsers
    if not blob:
        blob = b"A"
    elif blob[-1:] in (b"\n", b"\x00"):
        blob = blob[:-1] + b"Z"
    return blob
